6, Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial court, plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 136 of 1.986 before the learned District Judge, Naogaon, On transfer it was .heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, who allowed the appeal set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court, and sent the case back on remand to the trial court for retrial of the suit. Hence, this Rule has been issued, at the instance of the defendant-petitioners. 

 7. Mr. Shahidul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners submits that the learned Appellate Court has committed an error of law in sending the case back to the trial court, he contends that the Appellate Court is only allowed by law to remit a suit back to the trial court if the suit is disposed of by the trial court upon a preliminary point and the decree is reversed in appeal by the appellate Court but here in this case the suit has been disposed of on merit. 

 9. Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff- opposite parties firstly, submits that the learned trial Court has committed an error of law in accepting the report of the advocate commissioner without giving the plaintiff opportunity to cross examine the advocate commissioner on his report and thereby erroneously observed that the Madrsha was closed on 20.11. 81 and its assests worth at Tk. 10,000 / - was transferred to some other place by the defendants and thereby held that the suit was infructuous. In support of his contention that the acceptance of the advocate commissioner report was not law full he refers to the division of the case of Ad wait Charan Gope-Vs- Kadar Uddin, reported in 7 DLR 598, wherein it has been observed that: 

 "It is now too well established to be doubted that the commissioner's report is merely evidence in the case, although generally accepted; if the commissioner has performed his duties carefully and satisfactorily, and is in no way binding upon the court. The weight to be attached to such evidence must the depend on the facts and circumstances of acryl case and the other evidence, If any, adduced in the case." 

 10. The suit was filed on 14.9.81 accordingly, even if the Madrasha was as reported by the advocate commissioner, closed on 20.11.81 the cause of action for the suit was very much present at the time of the filing of the suit on 14.9.81 and when the order for ad-interim injunction was passed. The plaintiffs also filed miscellaneous case No. 252 of 1989 for violating the order of injunction passed by the learned trial court but the trial court did not dispose of the said Miscellaneous case prior to the disposal of the main suit. Further the trial court has dismissed the suit without considering the deposition of the plaintiff and papers filed by him. In view of the above the learned appellate court had reasons to set aside the judgment of the trial Court. The learned Appellate Court in his elaborate judgment discussed the necessity of taking further evidence for the pronouncement of the judgment and for proper adjudication of the suit. 

 11. But it has got to be considered whether the order for remand passed by the Appellate court for re-trial of the case by the trial court has been validly done or not. 

 12. Order 41 Rule 23 to 29 specifically deal with the provision of remanding a case by the appellate Court to the trial court. Rule 23 provides that if a suit is deposed of by the trial court upon a preliminary point and the decree passed by the trial court, is reversed in appeal, the Appellate Court may, .by order remand the case for hearing and disposal on merit. 

 13. But in the instant case, the trial court has disposed of the suit on merit. As per provisions of Rule 25 the appellate court may, if necessary frame issues and refer the same to the trial court and direct such court to take additional evidence required; but in that case the trial court shall proceed to try such issues and shall return the evidence to the appellate court together with its findings thereon and the reasons therefor, Thereafter the Appellate Court shall dispose of the Appeal in accordance with the provisions of Rule 26 of the aforesaid order. 

 14. Further if the appellate court requires any document to be produced or any witness to be examined to enable it to pronounce judgment or for any other substantial cause the appellate court may allow evidence or document to be produced or witness to be examined and in such a case as per order 41, Rule 28 the Appellate Court may either take such evidence or may direct the trial court take such evidence and, to sent it when taken, to the Appellate Court, order for remand should not be made under section 151 C.P.C. When there is any specific provision in the code which would meet the necessity of the case. No remand under section 151 C.P.C be given to give case a second opportunity to prove a 

 15. The appellate Court in the instant case has felt the necessity of taking additional evidence specially on point of advocate commissioners report but that the suit cannot be remanded to the trial court for re-trial. The appellate court may take such additional evidence itself or cause it to be taken by the trial court to send it to the appellate court as has been discussed above. For the reasons stated above the order of remand of the case for re-trial cannot be sustained law. 

 The suit was filed long ago in the year 1981 and under the facts and circumstances of the case it would be proper and lawful if appellate court takes the additional evidence itself and dispose of the appeal in accordance with law.
